source.title: Relative Representations: Topological and Geometric Perspectives
source.authors: Alejandro García-Castellanos; Giovanni Luca Marchetti; Danica Kragic; M. Scolamiero

record.tranche_reason: Tests relative-representation model stitching in a cross-language natural-language task, and evaluates modified relative transformations in that setting.
record.gate_note: The paper measures task performance when using one model's representation with a head from another model. Background claims about representational universality are cited, not tested. The death-time plots concern within-model class topology, not alignment between models, so they are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: Reports zero-shot cross-language stitching of fine-tuned RoBERTa encoders and heads via relative representations (Table 1, Table 2). These results directly measure how well one model's representation works with another model's head. That bears on V4, although the paper's aim is to improve the method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the normalized (robust) relative transformation substantially improves cross-language zero-shot stitching over the original one, and that topological densification (pre- and post-relative combined) adds a slight further gain. They also report that robust relative slightly beats Absolute in-domain in low-data settings. They note the robust version trades invariance to non-permutation isometries for invariance to non-isotropic rescalings.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the relative-representation transformation for zero-shot stitching, but adds Gaussian normalization and evaluates topological densification during fine-tuning; task and setting are a low-data English/French rating task with RoBERTa models.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with the relative-transformation variant and topological-densification setup. The authors report that pre-relative and post-relative densification alone hurt performance, while combining them performed best.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the II edition of the Workshop on Unifying Representations in Neural Models (UniReps 2024)
record.problems: Evidence is limited to one natural-language rating task, two languages, a 1% subsample of the Amazon Reviews dataset, and 5 experimental runs. The text describes the robust transformation's cross-domain performance as improved but does not establish broad interchangeability across model families or tasks.
record.rows_left_out: No table results left out. Figures 4-6 and the associated death-time observations were omitted because they describe topology within representations, not cross-model alignment or stitching performance relevant to the tested version.

untested.parts: No seed comparison of features or subspaces.

Only RoBERTa encoders, one rating task, en/fr. Encoders are fine-tuned with the relative layer in place and use translated paired anchors. Untested: linear maps, layer stitching, unpaired mapping, models trained independently without the relative layer, and other architectures.
No comparison of similarity measures or OOD inputs.
No test of completeness or causes of alignment.

missing.what: Absolute fr-head/en-encoder cross swap: Acc 24.96±9.27, F1 23.19±8.12, MAE 132.35±24.01. These appear only as baselines in r13-r15.
Absolute fr/fr reference (Acc 49.26, F1 48.74, MAE 63.89). This is the needed reference for judging stitching loss with the fr encoder.

record.verdict_notes: The record's baselines for cross-language rows compare methods (vs Absolute cross swap, or vs Robust without densification). They do not compare against the non-stitched model with the same encoder, which is what 'little loss' in V4 requires. I re-judged states against that reference. Same-domain rows are not stitching and are unlinked. Interchangeability here is partly engineered: both models are fine-tuned end-to-end with the relative layer, share the RoBERTa architecture and pretraining, and use translated paired anchors. Support is therefore narrow.

versions.untested_parts: No model scale or capability sweep, nor measurement of representation alignment as size or performance changes.
The task uses text in English and French, not paired image-caption representations; no alignment-versus-performance trend is measured.
No comparison across initialization seeds for shared features, units, or subspaces.

Tests relative transformations for stitching RoBERTa-based models in one rating task and two languages only; does not test layer stitching, relative representations without paired anchors, or other mapping approaches.
No recurrence of interpretable features or circuits is measured.
Does not compare representation-similarity measures, their settings, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution alignment.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment, or measure how complete or plateaued alignment is.

source_check.notes: The explicitly named Absolute cross-swap and without-densification baselines are valid method controls, except r39; interpreting stitching loss requires same-method non-stitched references. All metrics are multiplied by 100; the supplied text is v3 dated 2025-10-24.

statements.correction: Table 1: Vanilla en/fr F1=31.15; fr/fr Vanilla F1=35.33; fr/fr Absolute F1=48.74. Vanilla fr/en F1=20.86; en/en Vanilla F1=23.50; en/en Absolute F1=58.27. Robust en/fr F1=50.13; fr/en F1=60.18. V4 verdict for Vanilla: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The numbers are correct, but the references 48.74 and 58.27 are non-stitched Absolute models. Their differences from Vanilla stitched scores combine changes in training/interface with stitching. The study supports a method-dependent limitation rather than an unqualified challenges label.
